reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes precipitation in fcc-based HEAs (Al0.7CoCrFeNi and an fcc matrix alloy) under different conditions, not in the BCC TiVNbTa system. No evidence is provided that aging TiVNbTa at 700°C produces coherent nanoprecipitates, strengthens the alloy at 1273 K, or retains ductility. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Aging at ~700°C for 4 h can induce fine, coherent nanoprecipitates in single-phase BCC TiVNbTa.
Such nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion and inhibit recovery/recrystallization at 1273 K.
Precipitation strengthening will enhance yield strength at 1273 K beyond the 330 MPa baseline.
The aged alloy will retain sufficient ductility for the W-to-CuCrZr interface application.
The treatment will not trigger unwanted phase transformations that degrade thermal conductivity or ductility.
